sections.body:
Kindness means doing something that helps another person. That is all. It is a set of small actions, not a special kind of person.

Some kindness is obvious. You share your snacks. You help a friend who has fallen over. You say please and thank you.

Most kindness is tiny. You move your bag so somebody can sit down. You give back the pencil you borrowed. You wait with a child who is waiting for an adult.

Kindness has two parts. The first is **noticing**. You see that somebody needs something. The second is **doing** something about it. Both parts are needed. If you notice but do nothing, the need is still there.

Some people think kindness means being nice all the time. It does not. Kindness means doing the kind thing in the moment, even when you are cross, tired or busy. Sometimes the kind thing is the hardest one, and that is the one that counts.

And here is the good news. Kindness makes you feel warm inside, and people remember it. A kind child is trusted sooner and invited sooner.
examples: Let me move my bag so you can sit.
I noticed you were sad, so I sat with you.
Here, you can use my pencil.
sections.heading: What kindness is

sections.body:
Look at a normal school day. Kindness is already happening in it, if you know where to look.

With words. You say thank you when somebody helps you. You ask how somebody is. You tell your friend you liked the drawing they made.

With your face. A smile when somebody tells you a funny thing. A nod to show you are listening. Looking at somebody when they speak.

With your hands. You hold the door. You pass the salt. You pick up the paper that fell on the floor.

With your time. You play a game even when you would rather do something else. You listen to the whole story, not only the funny part.

With your voice. There is a kind way and an unkind way to say the same sentence. "That is wrong" is unkind. "I do not think that is right, because..." is kind. Same idea, different sound.

Kindness also works on grown-ups. They get tired too. "You look tired today" is a kind sentence for a teacher or a parent. And when they are cross, a quiet word helps more than a loud one.
examples: That is a really nice drawing.
You look tired today. Are you okay?
sections.heading: Kindness in ordinary moments

sections.body:
Sometimes a child stands alone by the wall. Nobody is being mean. They are simply not in the game yet. Here is how to bring them in.

One. Look. Notice the child with nobody to play with. Do not look away.

Two. Go over. Walk to them. Stand near them, close enough to talk.

Three. Ask. Ask about what they like. "Do you want to play with us?" is enough. You do not need a long speech.

Four. Include. If they say yes, give them a real job in the game. Not a fake one. "You are the goal keeper" is better than "you can watch".

Five. Keep going. If they say no, say okay and walk away. Do not push. Being left out feels bad, but so does being forced.

Six words are enough to start: "Do you want to join us?" Children who ask that question make a class kinder, one game at a time.
examples: Do you want to join us?
You can be the goal keeper.
That is okay. Maybe next time.
sections.heading: How to help somebody who is left out
steps: Look for the child who is playing alone.
Walk over and stand near them.
Ask if they want to play.
Give them a real job in the game.
Accept no, and walk away kindly.

sections.body:
These are the words for kindness. Learn them and you can be kind in a way other people understand.

Kind describes an action that helps somebody else. Kind is about what you do, not about what you are.

A **compliment** is a nice thing you say about what somebody did or made. A real compliment names something true.

To **invite** means to ask somebody to join you, and to accept it when they say no.

To **include** means to make room for somebody in the group, in the game or in the talk.

Try saying each word out loud. Then use one of them today, with a real person.
sections.heading: The kind words, one by one

terms.example: That was kind of you to wait for me.
terms.gloss: Doing something that helps somebody else. It describes what you do.

terms.example: I gave her a compliment about her picture.
terms.gloss: A nice thing you say about what somebody did or made.

terms.example: I invited him to sit with us.
terms.gloss: To ask somebody to join you, and to accept it when they say no.

terms.example: We included the new boy in our game.
terms.gloss: To make room for somebody in the group, the game or the talk.

sections.body:
Sometimes being kind is not easy. Here are the hard moments, and what to do.

You do not want to. You are busy, or tired, or it is raining and you want to stay in. Be kind anyway, in the smallest way. Bring the book your friend left. Give them a wave.

You are cross. You can be cross and kind at the same time. "I am cross with you, but I am still going to help you" is a true sentence.

You cannot do everything. You cannot fix every sad feeling. That is not your job. Your job is to be there and to tell a grown-up when something is really wrong.

You get it wrong. You say something unkind by accident. That happens. The kind thing to do is to say sorry straight away: "I am sorry, that was unkind of me." A sorry that is said quickly is worth more than a sorry said never.

Somebody is unkind to you. You do not have to be unkind back. You can say "That hurt my feelings" and walk to a grown-up. Being kind is not being weak, and it is not staying where you are being hurt.
examples: I am cross with you, but I will still help you.
I am sorry, that was unkind of me.
That hurt my feelings. I am going to tell my teacher.
sections.heading: When being kind is hard

sections.body:
We spend a lot of time being kind to other people. It is easy to forget to be kind to ourselves.

You can be kind to yourself in small ways. Say the sentence you would say to a friend. "That was hard. I did my best." Talk to yourself the way you talk to somebody you love.

You can also be kind to yourself by stopping. A rest is not lazy. A quiet minute is not wasted time. Your body needs sleep, food, water and quiet, just like everybody else's.

If you do something wrong, being kind to yourself does not mean pretending it was fine. It means you do not punish yourself for days. You fix what you can, you say sorry where you need to, and then you move on.

Kind children are not perfect children. They are children who try, and who keep trying. That is the whole secret.
examples: That was hard, and I did my best.
I am going to rest for a minute.
I made a mistake, and I am learning.
sections.heading: Kindness to yourself counts too

item.summary: Kindness is a set of small actions, not a special kind of person. After reading this, you can spot kindness in ordinary moments, welcome somebody who is left out, give a real compliment, and be kind to yourself on a hard day.
item.title: Being Kind to Others
